subject: Intermittent 504/timeout spike from ember-lite model — customer notice & postmortem
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@redflame.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: ops@redflame.ai
Date: 2026-11-16T22:05:12Z
Subject: Re: production errors — ember-lite timeouts

Hi Rishi,

We started seeing a clear uptick in 504/timeouts for requests routed to the ember-lite model around 21:52 UTC tonight. Roughly 2-3% of requests are failing with a 504; attached are three example request IDs and a short error snippet from our side: request ids (rfl-req-41a3, rfl-req-41b9, rfl-req-41c5). The failures are concentrated on long-context generation (>= 3k tokens) and happen across regions but primarily our us-east-1 traffic.

Can you confirm if anything changed on your side (kernel changes, quantization toggles, routing) and whether there's a mitigation we can apply? This is impacting our chat feature in a few customer-facing sessions — we may need fallback routing until this stabilizes.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Platform Engineering
RedFlame Health

Attachments: error-log-2026-11-16.txt (text)
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@redflame.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-16T22:18:40Z
Subject: Re: production errors — ember-lite timeouts

Elena — thanks for the heads up and the sample IDs. We're looking into it now. I see matching 504 spikes in our telemetry beginning ~21:45 UTC and a corresponding tail-latency increase on the ember-lite serving pool.

Immediate steps:
- Routing: we'll open a temporary routing policy to divert 20% of ember-lite traffic to ember-lite-v2-quant (compatibility tested) to reduce pressure.
- Instance scaling: ops is provisioning a small burst of extra replicas in us-east-1.
- Investigation: engineering will triage kernel selection and KV cache hit rates for long-context requests; I'll loop a short update in 30–45 minutes.

Looping Ben (customer lead) and Naomi (CS) so they can coordinate communications.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Update: ember-lite 504 spike — mitigation in place

Elena — quick update from our side:
- We've provisioned +3 replicas in your primary region (us-east-1) and enabled a 20% divert to ember-lite-v2-quant. Early telemetry shows the visible 504 rate falling from ~2.8% -> ~0.9% for your traffic.
- Root cause hypothesis: a kernel-selection regression in last week's runtime rollout that increases tail-latency for long-context (>3k tokens) requests and triggers timeouts on some shards. Engineering is validating metrics and a targeted rollback/patch.
- Next steps: we will either revert the kernel-selection change for ember-lite or ship a patch to kernel selector by EOD tomorrow (2026-11-17). I'll confirm an ETA in the morning and share a short postmortem once we have the RCA.

As a goodwill gesture we will apply a 10% usage credit for the affected time window; Ben will follow up with the formal credit note and any contract impacts.

Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as a Sev-2 and will keep you updated.

—Rishi

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Date: 2026-11-17T18:32:00Z
Subject: Postmortem: ember-lite 504 spike on 2026-11-16 (INC-4521)

Elena — summary postmortem and permanent fix plan for the ember-lite 504 spike. Thanks for your patience — below is a concise timeline, root cause, impact, and action items. Full writeup + logs are linked.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-11-16 21:45 — first telemetry spike (elevated tail-latency on ember-lite pool)
- 2026-11-16 22:22 — +3 replicas scaled in us-east-1; 22:25 routing divert deployed (20%)
- 2026-11-16 23:00 — visible error-rate reduced to ~0.9%
- 2026-11-17 09:15 — engineering reproduced issue in canary and confirmed kernel-selection regression
- 2026-11-17 12:40 — patch validated in canary (kernel selector fallback per-shard)
- 2026-11-17 16:05 — patch rolled to production with staged rollout; errors returned to baseline by 16:45

Root cause:
- A change in the serving runtime's kernel-selection heuristic (rolled as part of a weekly performance tuning A/B) caused an incompatible kernel path to be selected for some ember-lite weight shards when sequence lengths > 3k tokens. This produced longer tail-latencies on affected shards and a higher rate of request timeouts (504s) under typical client timeout windows.

Immediate remediation performed:
- Temporary traffic diversion to ember-lite-v2-quant and +3 replica scaling reduced customer-visible impact within ~30 minutes.
- Engineering implemented a per-shard kernel-selector fallback that forces the previously stable kernel path for long-context requests and validated the fix in canary.
- Full patch rolled to production with staged rollout by 2026-11-17 16:05 UTC.

Permanent actions and owners:
- Revert/adjust kernel-selection heuristics for long-context paths until further performance validation (owner: infra/serving runtime team, ticket INC-4521).
- Add canary test that runs long-context (>=3k tokens) generation workload as part of every kernel-selector rollout (owner: QA/CI).
- Dashboard alerting: new alert on per-shard tail-latency for sequences > 2k tokens (owner: observability).
- Customer communications: Ben will send formal credit confirmation and CS note (owner: ben_carter).

Customer impact and compensation:
- Affected customer sessions: RedFlame Health (approx 2.8% of requests 21:45–22:30 UTC).
- Applied a 10% usage credit for the impacted window; formal credit note to follow.

Links and artifacts:
- Incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4521
- Postmortem doc: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/emberlite-INC-4521-postmortem
- Included attachments: error-log-2026-11-16.txt, grafana-emberlite-tail-latency-20261116.png

If you'd like a quick call to walk through the remediation or the patch details I'm happy to set up a 30-minute sync. Otherwise we'll continue to monitor and share a short follow-up once the new canary tests are in place.

Thanks again and apologies for the disruption — we take these regressions seriously.

—Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
